agree.reason: The letter is calm and specific, but it never offers proof (no invoices, no meeting date) and never shows that chains are out of reach, so a director who thinks this is the usual yearly complaint has little reason to change her mind.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the unsupported claim that a third of pharmacies will close and invents no numbers, but "lose money on a fifth of its work" stretches a loss on 20 generics to all plan prescriptions, "or go without" goes beyond the facts, and it leaves out the partial offset from brand-name drugs.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are only repeated and none is worked into a result, such as what $1.80 per fill means across 3,100 prescriptions or across 38 pharmacies, so the loss stays abstract.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is described only as members driving "farther"; the letter never says that in those 14 counties the nearest chain is more than 20 miles away, which is the fact that answers the idea that members have plenty of chains to use.

qualification.reason: The letter makes no hedged or conditional claims, so qualification doesn't apply here.

objections.reason: Neither of her objections is met: the yearly-complaint doubt isn't answered with the invoice offer or the two pharmacies ready to stop filling for plan members, and the chain-access doubt isn't answered with the 20-mile distance.

fit.reason: It is a one-page open letter with clear numbered requests tied to the July 1 renewal, which is the form and length the brief asked for.
